S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of developmentally inappropriate motor restlessness, excessive talking, interrupting, difficulty remaining seated or quiet, and related inattention that causes impairment in more than one setting. It is typically a neurodevelopmental condition with earlier-life traits that may become clinically visible or more impairing when structure, supports, or life demands change. It is distinguished from anxiety, mood episodes, or situational stress reactions by its chronic pattern of hyperactivity/impulsivity and distractibility rather than episodic changes in energy or mood.

patient.stressor_event: Revision of personal habits (dress, manners, associations, quitting smoking)
patient.stressor: Marie decided to overhaul her habits so she could be taken seriously for forklift and CNC certification, including quitting nicotine breaks, changing how she presented herself at work, and trying to limit casual shop-floor conversations. During the following 1 year and 2 months, the stricter expectations and loss of informal movement breaks exposed a persistent pattern: she struggled to stay with inventory logs, became pulled off task by noise and activity on the line, forgot routine steps, left her station when she was expected to remain in place, and repeatedly interrupted coworkers during handoffs. What had once been manageable in a lower-pressure role became clinically significant when supervisors documented production errors, safety concerns, and conflict with teammates despite her strong motivation. She ultimately accepted an occupational health referral after a certification instructor told her the issue looked less like lack of effort and more like a treatable attention and impulse-control problem.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: When I'm doing inventory logs or reading the CNC training pages, I start out really trying, but after a few minutes the numbers or words blur together and I have to keep going back because I didn't take any of it in.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: On the line, one beep from another machine or somebody walking past with a pallet jack will pull my eyes and my whole brain away from what I'm doing, even if I know I'm supposed to stay on my own station.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: I forget normal stuff all the time, like clocking a step on the checklist, answering a supervisor's text, or bringing my safety glasses from my locker, and then it looks like I just don't care.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: If I have to sit for the certification class or a safety meeting, my foot is bouncing, I'm clicking a pen, picking at my sleeves, or shifting around so much people ask me to stop.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: What brought me in is I keep leaving my station or popping up during meetings when I'm supposed to stay put, and my supervisor says it's becoming a safety problem because I just take off before I even think about it.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: When I try to stand still by the machine or sit through training, it feels like there's pressure building in my body and I have to move, pace, stretch, or go do something right then.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Quiet stuff makes me feel trapped, like if I try to sit in the break room and read the manual, I end up humming, tapping, talking to somebody, or getting up instead of just being quiet.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: I talk way too much at work, especially during handoffs, and I'll keep explaining or joking even when I can see the other person is trying to get back to their job.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I cut in on people without meaning to, like jumping into coworkers' conversations or answering a question before the lead is done talking, and then everybody gets irritated with me.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_age_12_years: Even in elementary school, I was the kid who couldn't stay in my seat, talked over the teacher, and got notes sent home for blurting things out or wandering around the room.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: At work this has put my job and certification plans at risk, because supervisors have written me up for safety and production problems and coworkers are less willing to partner with me during handoffs.
add_requirements.duration: This has been causing serious problems for about 1 year and 2 months, ever since I tried to tighten up my habits and move toward forklift and CNC certification.
